source.title: Symbolic functioning and language development in children with Down syndrome.
source.venue: International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders

confidence_rationale: In 21 children with Down syndrome, symbolic play and symbolic comprehension correlated with expressive and receptive language but not with nonverbal ability (age partialled), which supports play-language coupling with specificity. But the coupling was strongest in younger children and the measures dissociated with age and language growth, which the authors read as language becoming domain-specific. That dissociation cuts against MECH-308's view that language stays a play-game rather than becoming a separate system. Small clinical sample.
failure_signatures: Small cross-sectional clinical sample (n=21) split into three age bands; the developmental dissociation is inferred, not tracked longitudinally.
Down syndrome has a specific expressive-language deficit profile, so the dissociation may be syndrome-specific.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Symbolic play and symbolic comprehension correlate with language but not nonverbal ability in children with Down syndrome; the association is stronger in younger children and weakens with age and language development, suggesting language becomes more domain-specific.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports MECH-308 at onset (play-language coupling specific relative to nonverbal cognition), but the age-dependent dissociation is a risk for the claim that language remains an instantiation within play_mode rather than branching into its own substrate.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Clinical population, cross-sectional age bands, symbolic rather than social play. The dissociation could fit a weaker MECH-308 (play bootstraps language, which then consolidates elsewhere) but not the strong 'not via a parallel language substrate' wording.
mapping.source_context: Children with Down syndrome aged 32-95 months; Test of Pretend Play, novel symbolic comprehension task, standardised language and nonverbal tests.

confidence_components.notes: Chosen as a dissociation case; low weight.
